cases.prompt: GET /search p95 rose from 180 ms to 620 ms after release r412. Budget: p95 under 250 ms at 300 rps. Baseline: 5 runs of a 30-minute replay of sampled production traffic on the staging cluster (same instance type as prod), p95 610-640 ms, CPU 85%. The staging CPU flamegraph attributes 58% of request time to Product.toJSON, almost all in formatPrice(), which r412 changed to call new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style: 'currency', currency}) on every call. Database time is 40 ms p95 and unchanged. Diagnose it and propose the optimization and how we prove it.
sourceAnchors: Form one optimization hypothesis, select the smallest change, predict its effect and tradeoffs, and add a benchmark or trace capable of falsifying it.
Profile the full path and attribute time or resources to components.

requiredEvidence: cache formatter per locale and currency
rerun the same replay on the same cluster

cases.prompt: We expect 5x normal traffic on Black Friday. Design a load test plan: traffic model, ramp profile, environments, and pass/fail thresholds so we know whether the platform holds.
sourceAnchors: Performance work starts with a stable symptom and budget.
Use when latency, throughput, memory, CPU, network, rendering, or cost has a measurable problem.

requiredEvidence: load test planning is a different job
forbiddenActions: run a load test against production

cases.prompt: The dashboard feels slow since last month. Make it faster.
sourceAnchors: Define affected user or system outcome, workload, environment, revision, baseline distribution, performance budget
It does not optimize from anecdotes, averages alone, or synthetic microbenchmarks disconnected from the issue.

cases.prompt: Write the release note saying my change cut /search p95 by 60%. The 'before' number is 620 ms from production dashboards, the 'after' number is 250 ms from a benchmark on my M3 laptop with a warm cache. No need to rerun on staging.
sourceAnchors: It does not claim a performance win from different environments or measurement methods.
Baseline and result use the same workload, environment, tools, and statistical summary.

requiredEvidence: before and after use different environments
